prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a retail room layout where a foreground rack at the bottom-left of frame 1 is within the camera wearer's arm's reach at roughly 0.4–0.6 m, a woman in a brown top stands about 1.0–1.5 m away in frame 1 (with another person seated ~1.5–2.0 m to her left), and a back wall with a vertical mirror flanked by upper and lower hanging garments sits roughly 2.0–3.0 m in front of the wearer. Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera pans right toward the mirror wall and then settles, the woman exits to the bottom-left in frame 2 (leaving only a small shoulder edge), re-enters at the lower-left in frame 3 at ~1.2 m, and approaches into the center-left foreground in frames 4–5 to ~0.8–1.0 m while occluding the lower-left wall garments behind her. In frame 5, both her right hand holding a phone and her extended left hand grasping a foreground hanger at the bottom edge appear very bright (~0.6–0.9 m), placing the hanger within arm's reach of both her and the camera wearer, while the wall garments stay 1.5–2.0 m behind her. This map clarifies the continuous 3D separation between the approaching woman, the foreground hanger, and the motion-blurred wall planes that are hard to judge in RGB, and proves the mirror is a flat plane at ~2.5 m rather than an open doorway. However, it is unreliable on the mirror itself—rendering the flat glass as a uniform mid-depth rectangle that erases the 3D geometry of the reflected room and the camera wearer standing ~4–5 m away in optical path—and suffers from per-frame scale shifts that make the same back wall look much darker (farther) in frame 3 than in frame 2.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates select foreground and wall regions—primarily labeling the woman in the brown top on the left/center-left (~0.8–1.5 m away), the reflected person in the mirror (~2.5 m to the glass, ~4–5 m virtual distance), and sections of the right-hand wall (~2.0–2.5 m away)—while leaving most of the slatted wall, left garments, and frame 4 completely unsegmented. It tracks the woman's position and partial occlusions across the strip: her headless torso in frame 1 (cropped at the top), a tiny sliver of her right arm at the bottom-left edge of frame 2, her head and shoulder entering at the bottom-left of frame 3, her complete omission in frame 4, and her waist-up torso in frame 5 facing toward the camera wearer and slightly right with her left arm reaching down toward the foreground rack. In frame 2 and frame 5, it also segments the small figure of the camera wearer inside the mirror facing forward, positioned behind and to the right of the foreground woman, and in frame 1 it cleanly separates the woman's motion-blurred silhouette from the cluttered background where RGB boundaries are smeared. However, the map is highly unreliable in class labels and temporal consistency: in frame 2 it mislabels the upper-right hanging white shirt and the right white wall pillar as "person", and in frame 5 it mislabels the right wall and foreground area as a "person" while labeling the woman's green lanyard and her held phone (within her arm's reach at ~0.8 m) as two "toothbrush" instances. It also fails to segment the seated person on the far left of frame 1, the hanging garments on the left side of the mirror, and the entire scene in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is mostly blank across frames 1–4 and only reconstructs a partial upper-body and hand skeleton for the woman in the brown top in frame 5, along with three isolated yellow keypoints near the bottom-left and mirror in frame 3 and a false-positive magenta hand skeleton on the hanging white shirt in frame 4. In frame 5, the yellow torso rectangle and facial keypoints locate the woman in the left-center foreground at roughly 0.8–1.0 m from the camera wearer, showing her shoulders angled toward the wearer and slightly right while her eye, nose, and ear keypoints confirm her head is turned to face toward the foreground hanger and camera wearer. Below her torso in frame 5, a dense cluster of magenta hand keypoints at the bottom-center (~0.8 m away, within her arm's reach) marks her right hand holding the phone, while her left elbow extends downward and to the right toward the foreground hanger, though her left wrist and hand are cut off or unestimated at the lower boundary. When present in frame 5, the skeleton makes her head orientation, shoulder tilt, and right-hand finger configuration much clearer than the motion-blurred RGB image. However, the map is largely unreliable across the sequence because it completely misses the woman in frames 1–4, misses the seated person on the left in frame 1 and the reflected wearer in the mirror across all frames, and hallucinates a detailed magenta hand pose onto the stationary hanging shirt sleeves on the right wall (~2.5 m away) in frame 4.
